elaphrosaurus:eswiki:8.title: Elaphrosaurus bambergi (Especies ya no asignadas a Elaphrosaurus)

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus was a medium-sized, lightly built dinosaur that could reach a length of 6.2 meters.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus was a medium-sized but lightly built member of the group that could grow up to 6.2 m long.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Elaphrosaurus bambergi was recovered from the Middle Dinosaur Member of the Tendaguru Formation in the Lindi Region of Tanzania.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Elaphrosaurus bambergi HMN Gr.S. 38–44 was recovered in the Middle Dinosaur Member of the Tendaguru Formation of Lindi Region in Tanzania.

facts.statement: Werner Janensch described and named the genus Elaphrosaurus and its type species Elaphrosaurus bambergi in 1920.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus was described and named by Werner Janensch in 1920 and the type species is Elaphrosaurus bambergi.

facts.statement: The genus name Elaphrosaurus means "light-footed lizard" in Greek, referencing its presumed high running speed.
facts.quote: The genus name Elaphrosaurus is derived from the Greek words (ελαφρός) meaning "light to bear" as in "light-footed", a reference to its presumed high running speed and "sauros" () meaning "lizard"; thus, "light-footed lizard".

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus measured approximately 6 to 6.2 meters in length, 1.46 meters in height at the hip, and weighed between 200 and 210 kilograms.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus was about 6 - 6.2 m long, 1.46 m tall at the hip, and weighed about 200 - 210 kg.

facts.statement: The tibia of Elaphrosaurus measured 608 mm, which was considerably longer than its femur at 520 mm, and its metatarsals were 74% the length of the femur.
facts.quote: The tibia (shin bone) of Elaphrosaurus, measured 608 mm was considerably longer than its femur (thigh bone) that measured 520 mm, and the metatarsals were 74% the length of the femur.

facts.statement: The limb proportions of Elaphrosaurus likely indicate it was adapted for running (cursorial habits).
facts.quote: These proportions, also shared by some ornithomimosaurs, likely indicate cursorial habits.

facts.statement: The cervical vertebrae of Elaphrosaurus were less flexible than those of other theropods, suggesting it supported a relatively small skull.
facts.quote: Although the neck of Elaphrosaurus was long, the thin zygapophyses and a lack of epipophyses on the cervical vertebrae indicate that it was much less flexible than those of other theropods and that it may have only supported a rather small skull.

facts.statement: Anatomical traits suggest Elaphrosaurus was not a predator of large prey and may have been omnivorous or herbivorous.
facts.quote: These traits argue against Elaphrosaurus being a predator of large prey, and it was possibly omnivorous or herbivorous due to its close relation with Limusaurus.

facts.statement: Recent studies by Carrano and Sampson (2008) and Carrano et al. (2012) classify Elaphrosaurus within the Ceratosauria.
facts.quote: More recent work by Carrano and Sampson (2008) and Carrano et al. (2012) assign Elaphrosaurus to the Ceratosauria.

facts.statement: A 2016 study concluded that Elaphrosaurus was an early member of the Noasauridae within Ceratosauria and formed a distinct group called Elaphrosaurinae.
facts.quote: A re-study of the known fossil material, published in 2016, concluded that, due to characteristics of the scapulocoracoid and metatarsals, Elaphrosaurus was actually an early member of the Noasauridae within Ceratosauria, and that it formed a distinct group with certain Asian noasaurids, which was named the Elaphrosaurinae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Elaphrosaurus was a carnivore, omnivore, or herbivore, with some researchers suggesting it was omnivorous or herbivorous due to its relation with Limusaurus.
facts.quote: It was possibly omnivorous or herbivorous due to its close relation with Limusaurus.

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus was noted by Paul (1988) as the longest-bodied and shallowest-chested theropod he had examined.
facts.quote: Paul (1988) noted that this was the longest-bodied and shallowest-chested theropod that he had examined.

facts.statement: A species named Elaphrosaurus iguidiensis was described by Albert-Félix de Lapparent in 1960 from Early Cretaceous sediments in Algeria, Libya, and Niger, but later studies deemed the assignment dubious.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus iguidiensis, was described by Albert-Félix de Lapparent in 1960, and the material was collected in Algeria, Libya and Niger in Early Cretaceous sediments.

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus gautieri was first described by de Lapparent in 1960 from Middle-Late Jurassic sediments at the Tiouraren Formation in Niger.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus gautieri, was first described by de Lapparent in 1960, and the material was collected at the Tiouraren Formation in Niger in Middle-Late Jurassic sediments.

facts.statement: The partial skeleton of Elaphrosaurus gautieri was renamed Spinostropheus gautieri by Sereno et al. in 2004.
facts.quote: This material, a partial skeleton, has since been renamed Spinostropheus gautieri by Sereno et al. (2004).

facts.statement: Stephan Pickering erected Elaphrosaurus philtippettensis in 1995 based on fossils from the Morrison Formation of Colorado, but later research concluded they are likely the coelurid theropod Tanycolagreus.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus philtippettensis, subsequently Elaphrosaurus philtippettorum, was erected by Stephan Pickering in 1995 based on USNM 5737, which consists of a tibia, a humerus, some metatarsals, and the distal portion of a fragmentary pubic bones recovered from the Morrison Formation of Colorado.

facts.statement: Dale Russell renamed Coelurus agilis as Elaphrosaurus agilis in 1980, but it is now considered a junior synonym of Coelurus fragilis.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus agilis, was a renaming by Dale Russell in 1980 of Coelurus agilis, originally named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1884.

facts.statement: Fossils from the Morrison Formation of Colorado were first referred to Dryosaurus in 1883 and later to Elaphrosaurus by Galton in 1982, but current knowledge places them in Ceratosauria incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus sp. USNM 8415, was discovered in 1883 and first referred to the ornithopod Dryosaurus. It was later referred to Elaphrosaurus by Galton in 1982, based on remains recovered at the Morrison Formation of Colorado.

facts.statement: Chure referred a fragmentary right tibia from the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation to Elaphrosaurus in 2001, but phylogenetic analysis suggests it resembles an undescribed abelisauroid theropod.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus sp. DMNH 36284, was referred to this genus by Chure in 2001, based on the proximal portion of a fragmentary right tibia from the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation.

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus bambergi lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 154 to 147 million years ago, in the Titonian stage in what is now Africa.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus bambergi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Elaphrosaurus de dinosaurio terópodo ceratosauriano, que vivió finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 154 a 147millones de años, en el Titoniense, en lo que hoy es África.

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus was elongated and slender with a long neck.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus era alargado y delgado, con un cuello largo.

facts.statement: Knowledge of Elaphrosaurus comes mainly from a single nearly complete skeleton, and no skull has been found.
facts.quote: Lo que se sabe sobre Elaphrosaurus proviene principalmente de un solo esqueleto casi completo y no se ha encontrado ningún cráneo.

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus measured approximately 6.2 meters in length, 1.46 meters in hip height, and weighed about 210 kilograms.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus tenía aproximadamente 6,2m, 1,46m de altura en la cadera y pesaba aproximadamente 210kg.

facts.statement: The tibia of Elaphrosaurus measured 608 mm, which was considerably longer than its 520 mm femur, while the metatarsals measured 74% of the femur's length.
facts.quote: La tibia, hueso de la espinilla, de Elaphrosaurus , medido 608mm, era considerablemente más larga que su fémur, el del hueso del muslo, que medía 520mm, y los metatarsianos medían el 74% de la longitud del fémur.

facts.statement: The limb proportions of Elaphrosaurus, shared with some ornithomimosaurians, likely indicate running habits.
facts.quote: Estas proporciones, también compartidas por algunos ornitomimosaurios , probablemente indican hábitos corredores.

facts.statement: The long tail of Elaphrosaurus ended with a rare downward curve that may not be related to taphonomy.
facts.quote: Su larga cola terminó con una rara curva descendente que puede no estar relacionada con la tafonomía.

facts.statement: Despite its long neck, thin zygapophyseal joints and lack of cervical epipophyses indicate Elaphrosaurus had a much less flexible neck than other theropods, likely supporting only a small skull.
facts.quote: Si bien el cuello de Elaphrosaurus era largo, las articulaciones cigapófisis delgadas y la falta de epipófisis en las vértebras cervicales indican que era mucho menos flexible que los de otros terópodos y que puede que solo haya soportado un cráneo bastante pequeño.

facts.statement: These traits suggest Elaphrosaurus hunted small prey and was possibly omnivorous or herbivorous due to its close relationship with Limusaurus.
facts.quote: Estos rasgos argumentan que Elaphrosaurus es un depredador de presas pequeñas y posiblemente fue omnívoro o herbívoro debido a su estrecha relación con Limusaurus.

facts.statement: The genus Elaphrosaurus was established by Janensch in 1920.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Janensch, 1920

facts.statement: Paul (1988) suggested that Elaphrosaurus bambergi likely hunted small and swift ornithopod herbivores rather than the larger sauropods and stegosaurs in its environment.
facts.quote: Paul (1988) noted that Elaphrosaurus bambergi was too small to prey on the sauropods and stegosaurs present in its paleoenvironment, and suggested instead that it likely hunted the small and swift ornithopod herbivores.

facts.statement: Newer studies support the idea that Elaphrosaurus was a herbivore or omnivore due to its close relation with Limusaurus and a neck less flexible than that of carnivorous theropods.
facts.quote: However, newer studies support the idea that Elaphrosaurus was a herbivore or omnivore, owing to its close relation with Limusaurus and a neck which is much less flexible than those characteristic of carnivorous theropods.

facts.statement: Studies suggest the paleoenvironment of the Tendaguru Formation was a marginal marine environment containing both non-marine fauna and flora.
facts.quote: Studies suggest that the paleoenvironment of the Tendaguru Formation was a marginal marine environment with both non-marine faunal and floral content.

facts.statement: The Middle Dinosaur Member of the Tendaguru Formation yielded sauropods like Giraffatitan and Dicraeosaurus, theropods similar to Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus, the carcharodontosaurid Veterupristisaurus, the stegosaurid Kentrosaurus, and the iguanodontian Dysalotosaurus.
facts.quote: The Middle Dinosaur Member of the Tendaguru Formation has yielded the sauropods Giraffatitan, Australodocus, Janenschia, Tornieria and Dicraeosaurus, theropods similar to Allosaurus and Ceratosaurus, the carcharodontosaurid Veterupristisaurus, the stegosaurid Kentrosaurus and the iguanodontian Dysalotosaurus.

facts.statement: Dinosaurs in this paleoenvironment shared the habitat with pterosaurs like Pterodactylus and Rhamphorhynchus, as well as early mammals.
facts.quote: Dinosaurs shared this paleoenvironment with pterosaurs like Pterodactylus and Rhamphorhynchus, as well as with early mammals.

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian stage of the Jurassic period, approximately 157 to 152 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue recolectado por Werner Janensch, I. Salim, H. Reck y Parkinson en 1910 en marga gris, verde, roja y arenosa que se depositó durante la etapa kimmeridgiana del período Jurásico , hace aproximadamente 157 a 152millones de años.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Elaphrosaurus bambergi was recovered from the Middle Dinosaur Member of the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Elaphrosaurus bambergi HMN'Gr.S.'38-44 se recuperó en el Miembro Dinosaurio Medio de la formación Tendaguru en Tanzania.

facts.statement: The genus Elaphrosaurus was described and named by Werner Janensch in 1920, with the type species being Elaphrosaurus bambergi.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus fue descrito y nombrado por Werner Janensch en 1920 y la especie tipo es Elaphrosaurus bambergi.

facts.statement: The genus name Elaphrosaurus means "light-legged lizard," derived from Greek words referring to its supposed running speed.
facts.quote: El nombre del género Elaphrosaurus se deriva de las palabras griegas elaphros, ελαφρός, que significa "piernas ligeras", una referencia a su velocidad de carrera supuesta y sauros, σαῦρος, que significa "lagarto, por lo tanto, "lagarto de patas ligeras".

facts.statement: The type specimen consists of 18 presacral vertebrae, 5 sacral vertebrae, 20 caudal vertebrae, a pelvic girdle, an almost complete left hind limb, several isolated metacarpals, and a humerus.
facts.quote: HMN'Gr.S.'38-44 consiste en 18vértebras presacras, 5vértebras sacras, 20vértebras caudales, una faja pélvica , una extremidad posterior izquierda casi completa, faltan solo algunas falanges, varios metacarpianos aislados y un húmero .

facts.statement: Werner Janensch originally described Elaphrosaurus as a coelurosaurian.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus fue descrito por primera vez por Janensch como un celurosaurio.

facts.statement: Franz Nopcsa placed Elaphrosaurus in the family Ornithomimidae in 1928 based on its light frame, straight and slender humerus, and low deltopectoral crest.
facts.quote: Luego, Elaphrosaurus fue colocado en la familia Ornithomimidae por Franz Nopcsa en 1928 debido a su marco ligero y al hecho de que su húmero es recto y delgado, con una cresta deltopectoral baja.

facts.statement: In 1990, researchers including Barsbold, Maryańska, and Osmólska still classified Elaphrosaurus as an ornithomimid.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 1990 Barsbold, Teresa Maryańska y Osmólska y otros investigadores todavía lo clasificaron como un ornitomímido.

facts.statement: A 2016 study concluded that Elaphrosaurus was an early member of Noasauridae within Ceratosauria, forming a group called Elaphrosaurinae with certain Asian noasaurids.
facts.quote: Un nuevo estudio del material fósil conocido, publicado en 2016, concluyó que, debido a las características de los escapulocorácoides y metatarsianos, Elaphrosaurus fue en realidad uno de los primeros miembros de Noasauridae dentro de Ceratosauria, y que formó un grupo con ciertos noasáuridos asiáticos, que fue nombrado el Elaphrosaurinae.

facts.statement: Elaphrosaurus includes only one species, E. bambergi, described by Janensch in 1920 from the Tendaguru Dinosaur Bed in East Africa.
facts.quote: Elaphrosaurus incluye solamente una especie, E. bambergi descrita por Janesch en 1920, del Lecho de dinosaurios de Tendaguru de África del Este.

facts.statement: In 1988, Paul observed that Elaphrosaurus was too small to attack sauropods and stegosaurs, suggesting it likely hunted small, fast herbivorous ornithopods.
facts.quote: Paul en 1988 observó que Elaphrosaurus bambergi era demasiado pequeño para atacar a los saurópodos y estegosáuridos presentes en su paleoambiente, y que, en su lugar, probablemente cazaba a los pequeños y rápidos herbívoros ornitópodos.

facts.statement: Recent studies suggest Elaphrosaurus may have been a herbivore or omnivore due to its close relationship with Limusaurus and a neck less flexible than typical carnivorous theropods.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios más recientes apoyan la idea de que Elaphrosaurus era un herbívoro u omnívoro, debido a su estrecha relación con Limusaurus y un cuello que es mucho menos flexible que los característicos de los terópodos carnívoros.

facts.statement: Dinosaur footprints from Niger and Jerusalem have been attributed to Elaphrosaurus, but this assignment is considered inconclusive.
facts.quote: Huellas de dinosaurios de la República de Níger y de Jerusalén fueron atribuidas a Elaphrosaurus. Esta asignación se considera no concluyente.

facts.statement: The time range for Elaphrosaurus extends from the Kimmeridgian to the Cenomanian, spanning from 154.8 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Cenomanian (154.8 to 93.9 million years ago)
